about.title: Ceres Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Defective products show up everywhere in Ceres life — a faulty ladder at a Whitmore Avenue job site, a malfunctioning appliance in a Mitchell Road apartment, a car part that fails near Hatch Road. California generally treats these as strict liability cases, meaning the injured person usually doesn't have to prove the manufacturer was negligent, only that the product had a defect and that defect caused harm. That's a meaningfully different path than a typical negligence claim, and it can involve manufacturers, distributors, and retailers all at once. Because Ceres sits within a busy agricultural and logistics corridor, equipment, machinery, and vehicle-related products come up often in local injury reports. If a product hurt you or someone in your family here, keeping the item itself and any packaging can matter a great deal later. We handle product liability cases and can review what happened to explain your options.

whyChoose.title: Why Strict Liability Matters for Ceres Residents

items.title: You Don't Have to Prove Carelessness
items.desc: Because California often applies strict liability to defective products, we may be able to build your case around the product's flaw itself rather than trying to show a company was negligent.

items.title: Multiple Parties Can Share Responsibility
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and retailers can all potentially be held liable under California product liability law, which may give your case more than one path forward.

items.title: Preserving the Product Preserves Your Options
items.desc: Since the defective item is often the central piece of evidence in a strict liability claim, we can advise you early on how to keep it safe rather than risk losing that evidence.

items.question: Do I need to prove the manufacturer knew about the defect?
items.answer: Not necessarily. Under California's strict liability approach, the focus is generally on whether the product was defective and caused injury, not on what the manufacturer knew or intended. We can explain how this applies to your specific situation.

items.question: What should I do with the product that hurt me here in Ceres?
items.answer: Try to keep the item exactly as it was at the time of the injury, along with any packaging, receipts, or instructions. Don't attempt repairs or throw it away, since it may be important evidence for a claim. Our team can advise you on safe storage once we've reviewed your case.

items.question: Do you handle product liability cases?
items.answer: Yes. We handle product liability matters and typically work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless there's a recovery.
